knowledge-base.overview: Rails 7+ guardrails, MVC patterns, ActiveRecord conventions, service objects, routing, migrations, and testing. Applies to full-stack Rails apps and API-only backends using PostgreSQL, Hotwire/Turbo, and ActiveJob. Convention over configuration: follow naming, directory structure, and RESTful route conventions at all times.

core-principles.principle: Follow Rails naming and directory conventions. A controller named PostsController maps to posts_controller.rb, views/posts/, and the posts table automatically.
Business logic lives in models and service objects. Controllers only handle request/response: set instance variables, call services, redirect or render.
Use concerns for shared model/controller behavior, partials for shared view markup, and service objects for reusable business workflows.
Design resources around the 7 standard CRUD actions before adding custom routes. Nest resources at most one level deep.
CSRF protection, XSS escaping, strong parameters, and parameterized queries are built in. Never disable them without documented justification.

guardrail.rule: Never use params.permit! — it allows mass assignment of all parameters. Always enumerate permitted attributes explicitly in a private *_params method.
Never use string interpolation in SQL queries. Use ActiveRecord query methods with parameterized placeholders.
Always use before_action for authentication and resource loading. Never inline auth checks in action bodies.
Always use includes/preload/eager_load when accessing associations in views or iterating. N+1 queries are a production performance blocker.
guardrail.bad: @posts = Post.published.recent # view: post.user.name => N+1 query per post

guardrail.rule: Keep controllers under 100 lines and each action under 10 lines. Extract complex logic to service objects in app/services/.
Always add null: false for required columns and database indexes for foreign keys and frequently filtered columns.
Always specify dependent: :destroy or dependent: :nullify on has_many/has_one associations. Unspecified dependent behavior causes orphaned records.
Never use raw or html_safe with user-provided content. ERB auto-escapes by default — only opt out for trusted, sanitized HTML.
Wrap multi-step database operations in ActiveRecord::Base.transaction. Partial failures must leave the database unchanged.
Use find_each instead of each when iterating large datasets. Model.all.each loads the entire table into memory.
Use status: :see_other (303) for redirect_to after DELETE actions to prevent resubmission on browser back.
Use render status: :unprocessable_entity (422) when re-rendering forms after a failed save.
Never modify a migration after it has been run in production. Create a new migration for corrections instead.

pattern.name: Model Ordering Convention
pattern.description: Always order model sections: associations, validations, enums, scopes, callbacks, class methods, instance methods, private methods.
pattern.example:
# app/models/post.rb class Post < ApplicationRecord # 1. Associations belongs_to :user belongs_to :category, optional: true has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy has_many :taggings, dependent: :destroy has_many :tags, through: :taggings has_one_attached :featured_image
# 2. Validations validates :title, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 } validates :body, presence: true
# 3. Enums enum :status, { draft: 0, published: 1, archived: 2 }
# 4. Scopes scope :published, -> { where(status: :published) } scope :recent, -> { order(created_at: :desc) } scope :search, ->(q) { where("title ILIKE :q OR body ILIKE :q", q: "%#{sanitize_sql_like(q)}%") }
# 5. Callbacks (keep minimal — prefer service objects for side effects) before_validation :normalize_title
# 6. Instance methods def publish! update!(status: :published, published_at: Time.current) end
private
def normalize_title self.title = title&.strip end end

pattern.name: RESTful Controller
pattern.example:
# app/controllers/posts_controller.rb class PostsController < ApplicationController before_action :authenticate_user!, except: [:index, :show] before_action :set_post, only: [:show, :edit, :update, :destroy] before_action :authorize_post!, only: [:edit, :update, :destroy]
def index @posts = Post.published .includes(:user, :category) .recent .page(params[:page]).per(20) end
def show; end
def new = @post = current_user.posts.build
def create @post = current_user.posts.build(post_params) if @post.save redirect_to @post, notice: "Post created." else render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity end end
def edit; end
def update if @post.update(post_params) redirect_to @post, notice: "Post updated." else render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity end end
def destroy @post.destroy redirect_to posts_url, notice: "Post deleted.", status: :see_other end
private
def set_post = @post = Post.find(params[:id]) def authorize_post! = redirect_to(posts_url, alert: "Not authorized.") unless @post.user == current_user def post_params = params.require(:post).permit(:title, :body, :category_id, :status, tag_ids: []) end

pattern.name: Routes
pattern.example:
# config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do root "home#index"
resources :posts do resources :comments, only: [:create, :destroy] member do post :publish post :unpublish end end
namespace :admin do root "dashboard#index" resources :users resources :posts end
namespace :api do namespace :v1 do resources :posts, only: [:index, :show, :create, :update, :destroy] end end
get "health", to: "health#show" end

pattern.name: Migration
pattern.example:
# db/migrate/20240115000000_create_posts.rb class CreatePosts < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1] def change create_table :posts do |t| t.references :user, null: false, foreign_key: true t.references :category, foreign_key: true t.string :title, null: false t.text :body, null: false t.integer :status, default: 0, null: false t.datetime :published_at t.integer :comments_count, default: 0, null: false t.timestamps end
add_index :posts, [:user_id, :status] add_index :posts, :published_at end end

pattern.name: Service Object
pattern.description: Use self.call pattern. Wrap multi-step operations in transactions. Return a result object instead of raising.
pattern.example:
# app/services/application_service.rb class ApplicationService def self.call(...) = new(...).call end
# app/services/posts/publish_service.rb module Posts class PublishService < ApplicationService def initialize(post:, user:) @post = post @user = user end
def call return ServiceResult.failure(["Not authorized"]) unless @user == @post.user
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do @post.update!(status: :published, published_at: Time.current) PostMailer.published(@post).deliver_later end
ServiceResult.success(@post) rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e ServiceResult.failure(e.record.errors.full_messages) end end end

pattern.name: Model Unit Test (Minitest)
pattern.example:
# test/models/post_test.rb require "test_helper"
class PostTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase def setup @post = posts(:first_post) end
test "valid post" do assert @post.valid? end
test "invalid without title" do @post.title = nil assert_not @post.valid? assert_includes @post.errors[:title], "can't be blank" end
test "publish! sets status and timestamp" do @post.publish! assert @post.published? assert_not_nil @post.published_at end end

quick-reference.item: associations, validations, enums, scopes, callbacks, class methods, instance methods, private
ActiveRecord methods or ? placeholders — never string interpolation
includes/preload/eager_load on every association accessed in views
self.call pattern; return ServiceResult; namespace by domain
find_each for large tables; never Model.all.each
Kaminari or Pagy on all list endpoints — never Model.all unscoped
ActiveJob + Sidekiq for email, notifications, heavy processing
Rails.application.credentials or ENV — never in source code
